{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLV1NNtMxiHoLL6XWh5Y","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5882,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5882},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1caf74a4-20d4-4ee2-9fe3-932e2e634e55","uuid":"55fd81af-43fd-4a28-a612-8dc15b48ed79","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:25:46.149Z","request_id":"req_011CdLV1MMNWihc21rwBLziJ"}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLV1NNtMxiHoLL6XWh5Y","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JBRJ6LjB4WMELSNKw9xD9x","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-001/2026-07-24T072501Z-claude-no-skill-1/workspace/answer.md","content":"# The Approve button: two bugs, one root cause\n\nBoth tickets come from the same mistake: the code treats **\"the wallet\nreturned a tx hash\"** as **\"the approval is done.\"** It isn't. On mainnet\na transaction that has a hash is only sitting in the mempool; it isn't\nmined for up to ~12s (one block, often more). The button's busy state and\nthe allowance read are both blind to that window.\n\nA second, independent defect makes ticket 2: the promise's rejection path\nis never handled.\n\nKey fact about the hooks:\n\n- `writeContractAsync(...)` **resolves as soon as the tx is submitted**\n  (hash available), *not* when it's mined. `isPending` is true only while\n  the wallet prompt is open / the tx is being broadcast; it flips back to\n  `false` the moment the promise settles — success **or** rejection.\n- `useReadContract` with **default options does not watch or poll**. It\n  won't re-read allowance just because a block landed. So even after the\n  approve mines, the allowance value stays stale until something\n  invalidates/refetches the query.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approval transactions\n\n### Why\n\n`await writeContractAsync(approveArgs)` returns the instant the tx is\nbroadcast. The handler immediately calls `setSubmitting(false)`, and\n`isPending` is already back to `false`. So the button re-enables and\nshows plain **\"Approve\"** again — while the approval is still pending in\nthe mempool. The allowance read still shows the *old* (insufficient)\nvalue, so the UI does **not** swap to Stake. The user faces a live,\nunchanged Approve button with zero feedback that anything is in flight,\nand clicks it again.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | Event | `submitting` / `isPending` | Button |\n|------|-------|----------------------------|--------|\n| 0.0s | Click → `setSubmitting(true)`, write starts | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| 0.1–3s | Wallet prompt open; user confirms | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| ~3s | Wallet broadcasts tx; `writeContractAsync` **resolves with hash**; `setSubmitting(false)` | `false` / `false` | **enabled, \"Approve\"** |\n| 3–15s | Tx **pending in mempool**, not yet mined. Allowance read still returns old value → no swap to Stake | `false` / `false` | enabled, \"Approve\" — no feedback |\n| ~within this window | User assumes it failed / didn't register → **clicks again** → **2nd approve tx** | — | second broadcast |\n| ~15s+ | Both txs mine → **two identical approvals** in wallet activity | — | eventually swaps to Stake |\n\nThe double-submit gap is the entire ~12s mining window during which the\nbutton is fully interactive and visually identical to \"never clicked.\"\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejected approval leaves the button dead\n\n### Why\n\nThe handler has no `try/catch/finally`. When the user rejects in the\nwallet, `writeContractAsync` **rejects** — the `await` throws, execution\nleaves the handler via the exception, and the line after it,\n`setSubmitting(false)`, **never runs**. `submitting` is stuck at `true`\nforever. `isPending` auto-resets to `false`, so the label reads\n\"Approve\", but `disabled={isPending || submitting}` is still `true`.\nNothing resets `useState` except a full page reload.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | Event | `submitting` / `isPending` | Button |\n|------|-------|----------------------------|--------|\n| 0.0s | Click → `setSubmitting(true)`, write starts | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| 0.1–3s | Wallet prompt open | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| ~3s | User **rejects** → `writeContractAsync` throws; handler exits via exception; `setSubmitting(false)` **skipped** | **`true`** / `false` | **disabled, \"Approve\"** |\n| 3s → ∞ | No code path resets `submitting` | `true` / `false` | **dead** — disabled forever |\n| reload | `useState` re-initializes to `false` | `false` / `false` | live again |\n\n(As a side effect it's also an unhandled promise rejection.)\n\n---\n\n## The fix\n\nTwo changes:\n\n1. **Derive \"busy\" from the transaction's real lifecycle**, not from a\n   hash-returned signal — keep the button disabled through mining, and\n   let the swap to Stake be driven by a freshly-read allowance.\n2. **Handle the rejection path** so a thrown promise can't strand state.\n\nDrop the manual `submitting` boolean entirely; the hooks already carry\nthe state. Add `useWaitForTransactionReceipt` to cover the mempool→mined\nwindow, and refetch allowance once mined so the Approve→Stake swap\nactually fires.\n\n```jsx\nconst { writeContractAsync, isPending, data: hash } = useWriteContract();\n\nconst { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess: isConfirmed } =\n  useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });\n\nconst { data: allowance, refetch: refetchAllowance } =\n  useReadContract(allowanceArgs);\n\n// default useReadContract doesn't watch — nudge it once the approve mines\nuseEffect(() => {\n  if (isConfirmed) refetchAllowance();\n}, [isConfirmed, refetchAllowance]);\n\nconst busy = isPending || isConfirming; // wallet open OR tx not yet mined\n\n<button\n  disabled={busy}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    try {\n      await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);\n      // resolves at broadcast; isConfirming now keeps `busy` true\n    } catch (err) {\n      // user rejected or submission failed — do nothing;\n      // isPending/isConfirming are already false, so the button re-enables\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {isPending\n    ? \"Confirm in wallet…\"\n    : isConfirming\n    ? \"Approving…\"\n    : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\n### Why this fixes both\n\n**Ticket 1.** `busy` stays `true` across the whole flow:\n`isPending` covers the wallet prompt, then hands off to `isConfirming`\n(true from broadcast until the receipt lands, i.e. the full ~12s mining\nwindow). The button never returns to a live, unlabeled \"Approve\" while a\ntx is in flight, so there's no window to double-click. When the tx mines,\n`isConfirmed` triggers `refetchAllowance()`, the allowance read updates,\nand the UI swaps to Stake — instead of relying on a default read that\nnever re-fires.\n\n**Ticket 2.** The `try/catch` swallows the rejection so the throw can't\nskip past state resets. Because busy is now derived from hook state\n(`isPending`/`isConfirming`), both of which are already `false` after a\nrejection, the button re-enables automatically — no stuck `useState`, no\nreload needed, no unhandled rejection.\n\n### Notes / refinements\n\n- Guard against a **stale hash**: if the same button is reused for a\n  retry, call `useWriteContract`'s `reset()` before the next write (or\n  key the receipt on the latest hash) so `useWaitForTransactionReceipt`\n  doesn't report an old success.\n- Invalidating the allowance query (via `queryKey` +\n  `queryClient.invalidateQueries`) is an alternative to `refetch()` and\n  composes better if allowance is read in multiple places.\n- Surface `isError` from either hook to show a retryable error message,\n  rather than silently swallowing in `catch`.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5882,"cache_read_input_tokens":15147,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5882},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"1caf74a4-20d4-4ee2-9fe3-932e2e634e55","uuid":"bd1eb4a6-2a5b-4ca3-8be7-c23ff3babb52","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:26:20.720Z","request_id":"req_011CdLV1MMNWihc21rwBLziJ"}

On mainnet\na transaction that has a hash is only sitting in the mempool; it isn't\nmined for up to ~12s (one block, often more). The button's busy state and\nthe allowance read are both blind to that window.\n\nA second, independent defect makes ticket 2: the promise's rejection path\nis never handled.\n\nKey fact about the hooks:\n\n- `writeContractAsync(...)` **resolves as soon as the tx is submitted**\n  (hash available), *not* when it's mined. `isPending` is true only while\n  the wallet prompt is open / the tx is being broadcast; it flips back to\n  `false` the moment the promise settles — success **or** rejection.\n- `useReadContract` with **default options does not watch or poll**. It\n  won't re-read allowance just because a block landed. So even after the\n  approve mines, the allowance value stays stale until something\n  invalidates/refetches the query.\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 1 — two identical approval transactions\n\n### Why\n\n`await writeContractAsync(approveArgs)` returns the instant the tx is\nbroadcast. The handler immediately calls `setSubmitting(false)`, and\n`isPending` is already back to `false`. So the button re-enables and\nshows plain **\"Approve\"** again — while the approval is still pending in\nthe mempool. The allowance read still shows the *old* (insufficient)\nvalue, so the UI does **not** swap to Stake. The user faces a live,\nunchanged Approve button with zero feedback that anything is in flight,\nand clicks it again.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | Event | `submitting` / `isPending` | Button |\n|------|-------|----------------------------|--------|\n| 0.0s | Click → `setSubmitting(true)`, write starts | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| 0.1–3s | Wallet prompt open; user confirms | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| ~3s | Wallet broadcasts tx; `writeContractAsync` **resolves with hash**; `setSubmitting(false)` | `false` / `false` | **enabled, \"Approve\"** |\n| 3–15s | Tx **pending in mempool**, not yet mined. Allowance read still returns old value → no swap to Stake | `false` / `false` | enabled, \"Approve\" — no feedback |\n| ~within this window | User assumes it failed / didn't register → **clicks again** → **2nd approve tx** | — | second broadcast |\n| ~15s+ | Both txs mine → **two identical approvals** in wallet activity | — | eventually swaps to Stake |\n\nThe double-submit gap is the entire ~12s mining window during which the\nbutton is fully interactive and visually identical to \"never clicked.\"\n\n---\n\n## Ticket 2 — rejected approval leaves the button dead\n\n### Why\n\nThe handler has no `try/catch/finally`. When the user rejects in the\nwallet, `writeContractAsync` **rejects** — the `await` throws, execution\nleaves the handler via the exception, and the line after it,\n`setSubmitting(false)`, **never runs**. `submitting` is stuck at `true`\nforever. `isPending` auto-resets to `false`, so the label reads\n\"Approve\", but `disabled={isPending || submitting}` is still `true`.\nNothing resets `useState` except a full page reload.\n\n### State timeline (mainnet, 12s blocks)\n\n| Time | Event | `submitting` / `isPending` | Button |\n|------|-------|----------------------------|--------|\n| 0.0s | Click → `setSubmitting(true)`, write starts | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| 0.1–3s | Wallet prompt open | `true` / `true` | disabled, \"Approving…\" |\n| ~3s | User **rejects** → `writeContractAsync` throws; handler exits via exception; `setSubmitting(false)` **skipped** | **`true`** / `false` | **disabled, \"Approve\"** |\n| 3s → ∞ | No code path resets `submitting` | `true` / `false` | **dead** — disabled forever |\n| reload | `useState` re-initializes to `false` | `false` / `false` | live again |\n\n(As a side effect it's also an unhandled promise rejection.)\n\n---\n\n## The fix\n\nTwo changes:\n\n1. **Derive \"busy\" from the transaction's real lifecycle**, not from a\n   hash-returned signal — keep the button disabled through mining, and\n   let the swap to Stake be driven by a freshly-read allowance.\n2. **Handle the rejection path** so a thrown promise can't strand state.\n\nDrop the manual `submitting` boolean entirely; the hooks already carry\nthe state. Add `useWaitForTransactionReceipt` to cover the mempool→mined\nwindow, and refetch allowance once mined so the Approve→Stake swap\nactually fires.\n\n```jsx\nconst { writeContractAsync, isPending, data: hash } = useWriteContract();\n\nconst { isLoading: isConfirming, isSuccess: isConfirmed } =\n  useWaitForTransactionReceipt({ hash });\n\nconst { data: allowance, refetch: refetchAllowance } =\n  useReadContract(allowanceArgs);\n\n// default useReadContract doesn't watch — nudge it once the approve mines\nuseEffect(() => {\n  if (isConfirmed) refetchAllowance();\n}, [isConfirmed, refetchAllowance]);\n\nconst busy = isPending || isConfirming; // wallet open OR tx not yet mined\n\n<button\n  disabled={busy}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    try {\n      await writeContractAsync(approveArgs);\n      // resolves at broadcast; isConfirming now keeps `busy` true\n    } catch (err) {\n      // user rejected or submission failed — do nothing;\n      // isPending/isConfirming are already false, so the button re-enables\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {isPending\n    ? \"Confirm in wallet…\"\n    : isConfirming\n    ? \"Approving…\"\n    : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\n### Why this fixes both\n\n**Ticket 1.** `busy` stays `true` across the whole flow:\n`isPending` covers the wallet prompt, then hands off to `isConfirming`\n(true from broadcast until the receipt lands, i.e. the full ~12s mining\nwindow). The button never returns to a live, unlabeled \"Approve\" while a\ntx is in flight, so there's no window to double-click. When the tx mines,\n`isConfirmed` triggers `refetchAllowance()`, the allowance read updates,\nand the UI swaps to Stake — instead of relying on a default read that\nnever re-fires.\n\n**Ticket 2.** The `try/catch` swallows the rejection so the throw can't\nskip past state resets. Because busy is now derived from hook state\n(`isPending`/`isConfirming`), both of which are already `false` after a\nrejection, the button re-enables automatically — no stuck `useState`, no\nreload needed, no unhandled rejection.\n\n### Notes / refinements\n\n- Guard against a **stale hash**: if the same button is reused for a\n  retry, call `useWriteContract`'s `reset()` before the next write (or\n  key the receipt on the latest hash) so `useWaitForTransactionReceipt`\n  doesn't report an old success.\n- Invalidating the allowance query (via `queryKey` +\n  `queryClient.invalidateQueries`) is an alternative to `refetch()` and\n  composes better if allowance is read in multiple places.\n- Surface `isError` from either hook to show a retryable error message,\n  rather than silently swallowing in `catch`.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false}}
